children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 17 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex. It's helpful to know he's 17 and living with you.

Since Alex is 17, I need to ask: is Alex currently in approved education or training? This would include things like:

- Full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar qualifications)
- Approved training programmes (not paid for by an employer)

Could you let me know Alex's current education or training situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex actually left school recently. He's been working with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next - you know, getting some guidance on his options and that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining Alex's situation. It sounds like he's currently between education and deciding on his next steps.

Just to clarify a couple of important points:

1. Is Alex registered with the careers service or a similar organisation for education or training? In the UK, this could mean he's registered with a Careers Service, Careers Wales, or a similar body.

2. Has it been less than 20 weeks since Alex left school?

These details will help me understand if Alex might still qualify while he's exploring his options.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - he registered with the careers service after he left school. And it's been less than 20 weeks since he finished, so still quite recent really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is very helpful!

I just have a couple more questions to confirm your eligibility:

1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Is Alex currently working 24 hours or more a week, or receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. And no, Alex isn't working that much - he's not doing 24 hours a week or anything like that. And he's not getting any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming those details. Based on everything you've told me, I have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarise your situation:
- Alex is 17 years old
- He lives with you in the UK
- He recently left school (less than 20 weeks ago)
- He is registered with a careers service
- He is not working 24 hours or more per week
- He is not receiving any benefits in his own right

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- You live in the UK and are responsible for Alex, who lives with you
- Although Alex is 17 and has left school, there is a specific provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for **up to 20 weeks** when a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service
- Alex meets all the criteria: he's registered with a careers service, it's been less than 20 weeks since he left school, he's not working 24+ hours per week, and he's not receiving benefits in his own right

**Important to note:** This eligibility lasts for up to 20 weeks from when Alex left school. After that period, to continue receiving Child Benefit, Alex would need to either:
- Start approved education or training, or
- Join the armed services

I hope this helps! If you have any other questions about Child Benefit, please feel free to ask.
